thesis: EchoStar (Nasdaq ticker changed from SATS to ECHO on June 24, 2026) has completed the bulk of its transformation from a distressed carrier into a deleveraged spectrum-and-SpaceX-optionality vehicle. On June 30, 2026 it deconsolidated its Pay-TV segment, booking a $9.7B gain that drove Q2 net income to $8.5B, while total debt fell 34% YoY to $17.4B and management pro-forma cash stands near $14-15B. The residual thesis is a sum-of-parts of remaining spectrum, a roughly 2% SpaceX equity stake, and shrinking Boost Mobile and Hughes operations. It is speculative because value hinges on SpaceX marks, the final SpaceX transaction close, and FCC-mandated Boost shutdown liabilities of $5-7B.

drivers: SpaceX equity stake re-rates as SpaceX/Starlink valuation climbs toward $1T+
Remaining mid-band spectrum monetized at premium valuations
Final SpaceX transaction closes, cutting debt a further ~$5B
Boost Mobile stabilizes as a capital-light hybrid MNO on AT&T
Market re-rates clean, deleveraged sum-of-parts to a higher multiple

base_case.assumptions: Sits near the ~$136 analyst consensus. SpaceX stake holds value; remaining spectrum retains strategic worth; deconsolidated Pay-TV no longer drags results; Boost and Hughes keep shrinking but at a manageable pace; FCC Boost-shutdown and tax liabilities land within the guided $5-7B; buybacks stay constrained by covenants near-term.

risks: SpaceX private marks fall or an IPO prices below expectations
Hughes and Boost subscriber losses accelerate further
FCC-mandated Boost network shutdown costs exceed the $5-7B estimate
Final SpaceX transaction is delayed, deferring the ~$5B debt reduction
Persistent negative free cash flow with buybacks blocked by debt covenants

catalysts.event: Final SpaceX transaction close — expected further ~$5B debt reduction
Q3 FY2026 earnings — first fully deconsolidated quarter
SpaceX / Starlink valuation and IPO developments — key sum-of-parts driver
Boost network shutdown execution and FCC milestones ($2.4B escrow set aside)
Further deleveraging and potential share-repurchase / dividend initiation

key_risks: Valuation is heavily dependent on the mark on EchoStar's ~2% SpaceX equity stake
Legacy businesses in secular decline — Hughes subscribers fell 24% YoY, Boost lost 118K in Q2
FCC-mandated Boost network shutdown plus tax liabilities estimated at $5-7B
Final SpaceX transaction must close to realize the further ~$5B debt reduction
Negative free cash flow and debt covenants currently limit the $5B buyback authorization
